title: First-Class Appendices for Print Reports and Zwischenbericht Anhänge
description: Add first-class appendix support to the semio print system (print/tex/): an appendix is a document attached to the main report, behaving like a chapter — numbered A, B, C…, labeled Anhang/Appendix, TOC entry, chip styling, cross-referenceable via \appendixref, listed via \listofappendices. Fix a pre-existing bug where window registers (\listoffigures etc.) render header-only because semio@render@register reads the wrong body macro. Wire the feature into all six print templates (report, paper, flyer n/a, zukunftbau forschungsbericht/zwischenbericht/kompaktbericht). Then apply it to mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht/zwischenbericht.tex: convert 9 Anhang markdown documents from temp/ into 8 LaTeX appendices (A-H), including a 67-project table with per-row avatar images sourced from temp/projekt_bilder/ (downscaled ~600px, copied into zwischenbericht/asset/projekt/). Update body cross-references to use \appendixref. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/print-reports-should-be-joyful-haven.md.
summary:
Fixed a genuine image-duplication bug: Photo/Table kind windows nested inside a WindowItem (WindowRow inside WindowArrangement — first exercised this session for the Projekte Katalog's Bild/Allgemein row layout) rendered their photo content twice, visibly doubled/offset (reported by the dev via screenshot for P.K.29, also reproduced for P.K.4, P.K.21, P.K.22).

Root-caused through extensive isolated tectonic reproduction (raw tcolorbox tests, bisecting `\semio_window_kind_begin:nnn` line by line, comparing against the working generic `\Window`-in-item path) down to a precise, narrow trigger: whenever a value derived from the enclosing tcolorbox's own fixed height (only reachable via WindowArrangement) also feeds into how large the image itself is drawn — via `\includegraphics`'s width+height keys, an equivalent `\scalebox` transform, even a heavily downscaled one — tcolorbox visibly typesets the box body twice. Confirmed via debug `\typeout` counting `\includegraphics` invocations. A plain `\rule` of the same rendered size, or any width-only image draw, never showed it — the trigger is specifically "does a height-derived value reach the image's own sizing," not the resulting size or which dimension binds under keepaspectratio.

Fixed by never letting that happen: added `\semio_image_graphics_itemclip:n` (semio-window.sty) — renders the image width-only into an sbox (never touching the box's height value for sizing), then clips the box to the target height via a TikZ path only if it overflows, using that height purely as a clip boundary rather than a sizing input. Wired into `\semio_image_typeset:n`'s "contain" branch whenever `\l_semio_window_in_item_bool` is set. Also kept the earlier, separate `breakable=false`-when-in-item fix for kind windows (matching generic `\Window`'s existing behavior) as a reasonable defensive improvement, though it was not itself the duplication's root cause.

Verified: rebuilt the full zwischenbericht clean (zero errors); visually swept all ~30 Katalog pages (all 67 projects) at high res — no duplication anywhere, and the two projects that previously overflowed badly with an earlier width-only-only fix attempt (P.K.21 Big Dig House, P.K.22 Saxum Vineyard Equipment Barn — both tall/portrait photos in a short row) now render cleanly clipped to their box. Rebuilt all 6 print templates (light+dark, 12 PDFs) clean with no errors, confirming no regression to the shared image pipeline used elsewhere in the print system.
